sentences.text: The genus name Doratorhynchus comes from Greek words meaning "lance" and "snout," describing the unique shape of its jaw.
This creature belongs to the suborder Pterodactyloidea, a group of pterosaurs characterized by broad wings and toothed jaws.
Harry Govier Seeley first collected a vertebra and a lower jaw from a quarry near Langton Matravers in late December 1868.
Richard Owen later named the species Pterodactylus validus in 1870, basing it on a thirty-centimeter-long partial wing finger phalanx found in the Purbeck Limestone of Britain.
In 1875, Seeley re-identified a previously classified tail vertebra as a cervical vertebra and erected the new genus Doratorhynchus for the species validus.
The re-identified cervical vertebra indicates that forms with very long necks existed during the Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous.
The fossil range of Doratorhynchus is recorded as extending from the Late Jurassic to the Cretaceous.
The Paleobiology Database lists Azhdarchidae as the parent group for Doratorhynchus.

Howse and Milner assigned the lower jaw specimen to the genus Gnathosaurus and the vertebra to an indeterminate ctenochasmatid. It was also suggested that Doratorhynchus was a basal member of the family Azhdarchidae.
